title: Māori-wording version control and authority-scope non-substitution gate
hypothesis: A nonbinding technical gate can record synthetic wording-version and mandate-scope transitions and can refuse substitution when an authorized Māori wording or authority review is absent, while never generating or ratifying Māori wording itself.
null_or_failure: Machine translation or paraphrase replaces authorized wording, a technical role is treated as Māori authority, scope expands without renewed consent, withdrawal is ignored, silence is treated as acceptance, or a synthetic artifact is called cultural ratification, legal interpretation, or enacted law.
test_falsifier_or_gate: Run synthetic version, paraphrase, translation, mandate-expansion, withdrawal, proxy-authority, data-governance, cultural, and legal vectors; require exact deferral and contain no purported Māori wording whenever authorized people are absent.
rollback_or_recovery: Stop the decision, preserve the prior authorized version reference without reproducing private wording, retain dissent and withdrawal, and defer to authorized affected parties, Māori authorities, Māori data-governance authorities, cultural authorities, and competent legal authorities.
boundary: No Māori wording is generated or ratified; all affected-party, Māori, cultural, data-governance, and legal authority remains external and exact-gated.
